pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.3 Handwriting (2 sessions) • Vocabulary: Descriptive words - colours •
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you ensure creativity in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme
2. appreciate different Arabic writing styles

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme

What this means
In this part you learn to create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate different Arabic writing styles

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate different Arabic writing styles. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate different Arabic writing styles. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: appreciate different Arabic writing styles)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Guided Writing: Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you ensure creativity in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme.
5. Be able to: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
